title: Rav Shmuel bar Idi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Taanit 9a](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.9a.14) it is told that Rav Huna bar Manoach, Rav Shmuel bar Idi, and Rav Chiya of Vostanya were frequently present before Rava. When he passed away, they came before Rav Papa. Whenever he told them a halakhic tradition and it did not seem reasonable to them, they would hint to one another. This pained him, and [the verse was read to him in his dream](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.9b.1), "And I destroyed the three shepherds." The next day, as they were taking leave of him, he said to them, "Let the rabbis go in peace" (so it appears in Ein Yaakov, and the intent is that he blessed them that they should live).[^1]
And in [Pesachim 104a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.104a.6), Rav Shmuel bar Idi sent word: "My brother Chananya says one" (and see the entry Chananya bar Idi).

But what we find in [Vayikra Rabbah 14:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Vayikra_Rabbah.14.2), “Rabbi Shmuel bar Idi said in the name of Rabbi Acha,” Hyman says should be corrected there to "Rabbi Shmuel bar Unya," as in Yalkut, Job, remez 902 (printed: תתקב).[^2]

notes.text: The dream and farewell continue onto 9b. The consulted Bavli reads bishlama. Hyman attributes lishlama to Ein Yaakov and explains it as a wish that the rabbis live.
Vayikra Rabbah has Rabbi Shmuel bar Idi speaking in the name of Rav Acha. Hyman gives Rabbi Acha and proposes reading Unya in place of Idi, citing Yalkut Shimoni.
